notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS059
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS059
**Contribute to the health, safety and wellbeing of students**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placementAssist in maintaining the classroom in a clean and tidy condition.

  - *Example: Wipe down tables as necessary using appropriate cleaning products.Provide guidance and support to students on the safe use and care of equipment and resources.*
  - *Example: Give students reminders/prompts on classroom expectations for use of equipment and resourcesSupport the provision of health promotion programs.*
  - *Example: Use specific program language in interactions with students.Provide assistance with the general care and wellbeing of students.*
  - *Example: Greet student with a smile and ask how they are.Provide health, safety and wellbeing information to students.*
  - *Example: Give students reminders about safety rules for example walking inside.Supervise students within the classroom according to teacher direction and organisation policies and procedures.*
  - *Example: Position self in the classroom for best possible view of students. Supervise students outside the classroom according to teacher direction and school policy and procedures.*
  - *Example: Show awareness of students who require extra supervision.Tasks to complete the written placement assessments:Locate the First Aid kit at the school.Locate and read schools policies and procedures that provide guidance in ensuring the health and safety of students.Locate and read schools policies and procedures on reporting a health issue of a student. SKILLS LIST*

notes.title: Skills List — HLTWHS001
notes.content:
# Skills List — HLTWHS001
**Participate in workplace health and safety**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.Consistently apply workplace safety procedures in the day-to-day work activities required by the job role

  - *Example: sign into the officeFollow workplace procedures for reporting hazards*
  - *Example: Adhere to the schools procedure for any hazards identified, i.e report to teacher, WHS representative Follow workplace procedures for any emergency situation*
  - *Example: Participate and follow procedures for emergency evacuation / lock downAdhere workplace policies and procedures for WHS*
  - *Example: Know where to access sites Policies and procedures, discuss with teacher / supervisor if neededIdentify workplace hazards relevant to the industry settings and respond according*
  - *Example: Through observations, any hazards are identified, eliminated and reported as per schools procedures to ensure duty of care is adheredRole model personal protective equipment (PPE)*
  - *Example: Wearing sun hat when outsideDemonstrate rights and responsibilities of employers and workers, including duty of care*
  - *Example: Staying in view of the teacher at all times, reporting any WHS concerns, HazardsTasks to complete whilst on placement:Assessment 2: As part of this simulated assessment the student is required to attend a three (3) monthly WHS meeting as required by the Wattle Grove Birth to Year 12 WHS Policy and procedures as outlined in Appendix 1 Meeting agenda1. Prior to attending the simulated assessment, the student must read through the assessment to ensure your understanding of the assessment criteria, including Appendix 5 WHS Policy and procedures and Appendix 6 Workplace emergency procedures2. The student must print a copy of the assessment to bring with you to complete the simulated assessment and hand up the completed assessment to the TAFESA Assessor at the conclusion of the assessment.3. The TAFESA Assessor will simulate a meeting area in the workplace in which the assessment will take place.4. As part of the agenda the student is required to complete a workplace inspection on existing hazards using Appendix 2 Hazard Checklist. and discuss these as part of the agenda. From the discussion in the meeting the student is required to use Appendix 3 Risk Matrix and5. Control Measures and add this to the Appendix 4 WHS Hazard report for one (1) existing hazard they have identified according to workplace policies and procedures6. As part of the agenda the student is required to engage in a discussion on potential hazards in the workplace. From this discussion in the meeting the student is required to use Appendix 3 Risk Matrix and Control Measures and add this to the Appendix 4 WHS Hazard report for one potential (1) hazard they have identified according to workplace policies and procedures7. As part of the Wattle Grove Birth to Year 12 WHS policy and procedure Appendix 5 the student will engage in a simulated emergency evacuation to ensure they have current understanding of the requirements for an emergency evacuation. As part of the meeting they will engage in discussion about the effectiveness of the simulated emergency evacuation at the conclusion of the simulation.8. An incident forms part of the meeting and the student is required to complete Appendix 7 Incident report as part of the Any other business on the agenda.The student is not required to upload any documents to TAFESA LEARN but will provide all completed Appendices below to the TAFESA Assessor for uploading· Appendix 2 Hazard Checklist· Appendix 4 WHS Hazard report· Appendix 7 Incident reportSKILLS LIST*

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS060
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS060
**Work effectively with students and colleagues**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.Use positive and respectful communication styles with two (2) students in all situations.Use positive and effective communication styles with one (1) ESW (Education Support Workers) in all situations.Demonstrate ability to respond to non-verbal cues with two (2) students.Demonstrate ability to respond to non-verbal cues with one (1) ESW.Demonstrate active listening techniques to explore student’s interests and concerns through conversations as appropriate (must be observed with 2 students).Demonstrate active listening techniques to clarify information (must be observed with 2 students and 1 ESW).Use communication styles with students that are developmentally appropriate to support interactions and problem solving.Show genuine interest in, understanding of and respect for all students in the class.Provide encouragement that acknowledges efforts and achievement, to build confidence (Must be demonstrated with two (2) students).Demonstrate calm behaviour and responds appropriately to students displaying signs of distress, frustration, or anger.Demonstrate use of initiative to support students as required and within ESW job role.Demonstrate consideration for the needs of student in all actions and decisions during learning activities.Support students to make own choices and experience natural consequences in a safe and supportive environment.Work collaboratively with ESW/teacher to share information following the school’s policies and procedures for sharing information.Work collaboratively with teacher/ESW to solve problems (e.g., not enough resources for students).Work collaboratively with students to solve problems (must be observed with 2 students).Use inclusive. communication styles that show respect and reflect the diversity (different cultural values, practices, and sensitivities) of individuals in the school to benefit educational outcomes.

- Tasks to complete the written placement assessments:While you are on vocational placement (or in your workplace), arrange to meet with ESW and teacher to seek feedback on your personal effectiveness in working with diversity.Question 1a) Write a summary of the feedback you received from ESW’sb) Write a summary of the feedback you received from teachers (teachers can include leadership staff)Question 2List two (2) ways you have acted on this feedback during your vocational placement to continuously improve your practice.SKILLS LIST

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS033
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS033
**Meet legal and ethical obligations in an education support environment**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.Working legally in accordance with scope of education support worker (ESW) role and organisational requirements.

  - *Example: When working with a student or a group of students, ensure that you have a teacher or a senior staff member present for supervision. TAFESA student works ethically in accordance with scope of education support worker (ESW) role and organisational requirements by:*
  - *Example: Treat all students fairly and do not discriminate based on religion, ethnicity or gender. Using open and closed questions and active listening to confirm and clarify information from a supervising teacher*
  - *Example: Use active listening skills e.g. clarify points, paraphrasing and use open and engaging body language, to ensure effective communication. Tasks to complete the written placement assessments.Task 1. As part of Assessment 2, arrange to meet with your supervising teacher early in your placement to have an induction using the TAFESA Students Site Induction Checklist.Task 2 – As part of Assessment 3, arrange to meet with your supervising teacher for verbal feedback to confirm your compliance with legislation and school policies and procedures. SKILLS LIST*

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS049
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS049
**Supervise students outside the classroom**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.Implement strategies and expectations for student behaviour as planned in the Activity Risk Report

  - *Example: giving reminders of expectations for behaviour before tasks supporting behaviour policy/plan, provide instructions in a clear and appropriate manner in accordance with behaviour policy/plan  Model positive interactions with students during the activity utilising verbal and non-verbal communication.*
  - *Example: use the name of the student throughout the activity, use active listening skills to demonstrate involvement, use respectful language Model positive interactions with adults during the activity.*
  - *Example: ask for clarification regarding a task within an activity, choose appropriate time and place to ask questions, uses the name of a staff member when confirming responsibilities Use verbal and non-verbal techniques to acknowledge and influence student behaviour during supervision of group activity.*
  - *Example: using short, clear and consistent instructions of expectation for activity, rephrases instructions as to what students should be doing Use supervision techniques to monitor area and students during the planned activity.*
  - *Example: arrange the environment for maximum visibility, accessibility, and flow space around equipment, listens for unusual sounds, crying or silence during activities, and continually scans the environment to know where everyone is and what they are doing Use planned strategies in a timely manner to prevent escalation of incidents during the planned activity.*
  - *Example: redirect student from an activity if behaviour is starting to escalate, work with students to solve problems that arise between themselves, Tasks to complete the written placement assessments:Assessment 2: Part 1: While you are on placement, you will need to access school policies and procedures to respond to the following questions. 1) Using the school’s behaviour policy, document a minimum of two (2) behaviour expectations that you need to communicate to students before implementing the activities. 2) What is the school’s communication process for gaining assistance? 3) a) If a student seriously injures themselves while you are supervising them, outline the school’s procedure you need to follow to report/document the incident/emergency? b) If a student seriously injures themselves while you are supervising them, outline the schools debriefing process you would follow? Part 2: Step 1: While on placement, you need to work collaboratively with your supervising teacher and conduct a risk analysis for two different activities; each one to take place in different locations outside of the classroom, with a group of students (minimum 5 per group). One of the activities must be a physical play activity such as PE, drama, supervised play, fitness Step 2: Before implementing the activities, you will need to assess the location of where the activity will be held and follow school policies to address the hazards identified. You will list these hazards on your plan (activity risk report Appendix 1). A total of two (2) templates must be submitted to Learn before placement observation visit occurs. Complete all sections of Part 2 of the Outside of classroom activity risk report (Appendix 1). SKILLS LIST*

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS035
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS035
**Contribute to student education in all developmental domains**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.Use positive communication to recognise and acknowledge differences in student learning styles.Use positive communication to recognise and acknowledge differences in student abilities.Use oral communication skills to interact, engage and build rapport with students.

- Use the planned support strategy (identified in Assessment 2) to support an individual student’s physical development.Use the planned support strategy (identified in Assessment 2) to support an individual student’s social/emotional development.Use the planned support strategy (identified in Assessment 2) to support an individual student’s cognitive development.Use the planned support strategy (identified in Assessment 2) to support an individual student’s language development.Use materials/resources (identified in Assessment 2) to support an individual student’s physical development.Use materials/resources (identified in Assessment 2) to support an individual student’s social/emotional development.Use materials/resources (identified in Assessment 2) to support an individual student’s cognitive development.Use materials/resources (identified in Assessment 2) to support an individual student’s language development.Tasks to complete the written placement assessments:For Assessment 2, Part A, meet with the teacher and ask them questions to prepare to support the development of two (2) students in the four domains.

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS036
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS036
**Support the development of literacy and oral language skills**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.Use communication skills to engage with students, build rapport and support positive interactions.Work within the structure and guidelines of the literacy program as directed by a teacher (during the literacy block in primary school or English lesson in secondary school).Implement support strategies as directed by the teacher to provide individual support to two (2) different students in oral language, reading and writing.Demonstrate a literacy concept to one (1) student and give them opportunities to practice.Select, use and modify literacy resources for two (2) students based on their individual needs during a literacy activity.Give students positive feedback that encourages and supports them to be independent learners.Provide clear directions and instructions to students.Tasks to complete the written placement assessments:For Assessment 2, meet with your teacher (a class teacher in a primary school or an English teacher in a secondary school) and ask the teacher about their literacy program.

- Record the teacher’s responses in the table (question 1).During the meeting with the teacher, ask them to identify two (2) students who you can support with their reading, writing and oral language.
- Ask the teacher about strategies they would like you to use in each area and record their responses (question 2).Describe a literacy activity where you will support the two students (question 3a).Evaluate student progress during a literacy activity by answering the questions in 4a and provide this information to the teacher in an email (question 4b).Meet with the teacher to review the effectiveness of the strategies you have used to support the students and ask for feedback and suggestions.
- Write a summary of the meeting and include one example of how you will adjust the strategies you use in the future (question 5).Find out about how confidentiality of students’ literacy records (electronic and/or hard copy) is maintained at the school (question 6).SKILLS LIST

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS037
notes.content:

**Support the development of numeracy skills**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.Use oral communication skills to interact, engage and build rapport with students.Use communication techniques that support effective interaction and learningProvide students with positive feedback to encourage the development of self-reliance in numeracyWork within the structure and guidelines of the numeracy program as directed by a teacher (during the numeracy block in primary school or maths lesson in secondary school)Implement support strategies as directed by the teacher (strategies identified in Assessment 2 - Q2c and Q3c) to provide individual support to two (2) different students.

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS034
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS034
**Contribute to the planning and implementation of educational programs**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.Source and organise resources, materials and student work to prepare for the implementation of an educational program.Direct students to the location of resources and materials that will be required during the implementation of an educational program.Guide students in the application/operation of relevant resources and materials needed to participate in the implementation of an educational program.Prepare and use relevant equipment, materials and resources required for the educational program.Clarify requirements with the teacher prior and during implementation of an educational program.Implement the strategies identified in the Educational Planning Template (from Assessment 2).Implement routine activities during the educational program (e.g. following set up or pack up routine).Follow and manage routine duties and tasks (e.g. tidying work area) within established timeframes according to school policies and procedures.Foster positive relationships with students using a positive approach whilst implementing an educational program.Foster cooperation through positive techniques whilst working with the supervising teacher and students.Make possible environmental modifications that suit the individual needs of students according to established guidelines (e.g. removing distractions, moving to a quiet area of the classroom).Tasks to complete the written placement assessments:For Assessment 2, Part 1, you will meet with your supervising teacher to plan how you will contribute to the preparation and implementation of three (3) different classroom educational programs.

- Each educational program will focus on the needs of one (1) student.
- You will complete a Planning Report template for each program.For Assessment 2, Part 2, you will implement the educational programs and record observations of the three (3) students identifying any individual learning needs and summarising the engagement and progress of the students.Part 3, you will self-evaluate the implementation of the educational programs planned in Assessment 2 and discuss your evaluations with your supervising teacher, seeking feedback to improve your practice.
- SKILLS LIST

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS057
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS057
**Support students with additional needs in the classroom**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.

- Support students with additional needs during whole class activities.
  - *Example: use various support strategies, get down to students’ level, repeat instructions   Demonstrate a commitment to access and equity principles in all work.*
  - *Example: use encouragement, show respect in interactions with students.   Use inclusive approaches to provide support to students.*
  - *Example: Use language suited to individual student needs, modify activities to meet individual student needs.  Provide encouragement which promotes students’ positive self-concept and self-esteem.*
  - *Example: Use questioning, positive reinforcement. Provide advice and feedback to students during the activity/lesson.*
  - *Example: Give students clear direction how to go about the tasks, respond appropriately to students. Show respect, empathy and acceptance for individual differences when interacting with students to build rapport.*
  - *Example: talk with students about their interests outside of school, include students in conversations. Use language suited to individual student needs.*
  - *Example: Use clear voice and language appropriate to age/development level. Use equipment and materials suited to individual student needs.*
  - *Example: Use resources suggested by teacher, become familiar with using equipment, resources and technology. Assist with required modifications of activities to meet individual student needs.*
  - *Example: Use initiative to make modifications to activities when needed. Respond appropriately to the effects of the additional need on the student learning.*
  - *Example: Modify language and resources to meet the student’s needs, follow guidelines set by the teacher. Use strategies to support students to guide their problem solving.*
  - *Example: Ask open ended questions to support students during activities/tasks, allow students time to process information and respond.  Uses strategies to develop independence.*
  - *Example: Provide students with time and opportunities to practice skills, encourage students to complete tasks independently.  Use opportunities to support and encourage incidental learning.*
  - *Example: Follow the students lead, use open ended questions. Use positive guidance strategies and techniques.*
  - *Example: Give students reminders, explain expectations clearly. Use strategies to develop student’s social skills.*
  - *Example: support students to interact positively with others, role model appropriate behaviours with students. Tasks to complete the written placement assessments. Assessment 2 Part A: Consult with your supervising teacher, to identify two (2) students with additional needs to support during two (2) different whole class activities/lessons. Complete one (1) observation (diary sample) of each student during a whole class activity/lesson and share with the teacher. Record in question 2 on the template - Learning Support Plan Ask your supervising teacher to sign the assessor other party report (AOPR) to verify that you collaborated with them to identify the additional learning needs of two (2) students, contributed to the planning of support strategies for the two (2) students and shared observations of the two (2) students. Assessment 2 Part B Ask your supervising teacher to sign the Assessor Other Party Report document (AOPR) to verify that you provided assistance during one (1) whole class activity/lesson and supported one (1) of the identified students. SKILLS LIST*

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS056
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS056
**Provide support to students with autism spectrum disorder**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.Support teaching strategies used by the teacher through modelling teacher’s practice

  - *Example: Model the support strategy the teacher is using to support learning for students; Support strategies used by the teacher for reinforcement*
  - *Example: Practice giving positive feedback to the student, being specific with what they have achieved/attempted; Notice the student’s cues when communicating with you. Practice responding in a way that is positive, encouraging yet being firm and friendly; Reinforce the directions the teacher has given. Use oral communication skills to interact and engage students to build rapport*
  - *Example: Use students’ names; Use positive communication to talk to the student about their interests and what they enjoy doing; Practice using open ended questions during communication. Eg: Tell me about……..; Practice active listening by using phrases such as: Are you saying that ………..?; Show an interest in what the student is saying.( Eg: use Ah ha, I see, that’s great, smile ); Use initiative to anticipate when it is necessary to support student with autism spectrum disorder by intervening or diverting the student.*
  - *Example: Practice breaking the teacher’s instructions down into manageable steps. Use words like: First, we are going to….., Next, we need to ……. Now, it is time to ………; provide alternatives if struggling with the situation; reflect on past achievements on how they can use this for this activity.Tasks to complete the written placement assessments.Assessment 2 Part 1 Consult with the teacher, to identify one (1) student who has been identified with autism spectrum disorder, who requires support to have positive social interactions. Discuss with the teacher the identified points in the Activity Template question 1 – 7 (Appendix 1) and record the responses.Ask your supervising teacher to sign the assessor other party report (AOPR) to verify that the planning meeting occurred and you used listening and questioning to seek the required informationPart 2 Ask your supervising teacher to sign the assessor other party report (AOPR) to verify that you prepared the two (2) learning resources and supported the selected student to have positive social interactions.Part 3 Make time with your supervising teacher to:report on the selected student’s progress in meeting the set goals for the activity contribute information for goal setting based on the selected student’s progress and your knowledge of autism spectrum. Ask your supervising teacher to sign the assessor other party report (AOPR) to verify that you met with them to report on the selected student’s progress and contribute information for goal setting for the selected student.SKILLS LIST*

notes.title: Skills List — CHCEDS041
notes.content:
# Skills List — CHCEDS041
**Set up and sustain learning areas**

> Select two (2) or three (3) of the skills below to work towards on each day on your placement.

  - Prepare and set up learning areas prior to the arrival of students according to teacher direction and school policies and procedures.
    - *Example: Arrange resources and materials on tables ready for use before students enter the classroom.*
  - Support teachers to create a positive and inclusive learning environment.
    - *Example: Help display student work and ensure the classroom reflects diverse cultural backgrounds.*
  - Assist with the organisation and maintenance of learning resources and equipment.
    - *Example: Return resources to their correct storage location at the end of each lesson.*
  - Support the maintenance of a safe and orderly learning environment.
    - *Example: Ensure pathways between desks are clear and free from trip hazards.*
  - Assist with packing up and storing resources at the end of learning activities.
    - *Example: Collect and sort materials, returning them to the correct storage area.*
  - Prepare and adapt learning materials under teacher direction to meet the needs of individual students.
    - *Example: Modify worksheets or resources as directed to support students with additional learning needs.*
  - Monitor the condition of equipment and resources and report any damage or need for replacement.
    - *Example: Inform the teacher when supplies are running low or equipment is damaged.*
  - Support the set up and pack down of specialist learning areas such as technology labs or art rooms.
    - *Example: Assist in setting up computers or art materials before a lesson and cleaning up after.*

- Tasks to complete the written placement assessments:
  Photograph or document two (2) examples of learning areas you have helped set up during your placement. Write a brief description of how each was organised to support the learning activity.
  Reflect on how the environment supports student engagement and learning outcomes.

SKILLS LIST
